title: 需求曲线与它的移动
titleEn: The Demand Curve and Why It Moves
lead: 价格变化是「沿曲线移动」，收入、偏好、替代品价格变化才是「整条曲线平移」。
leadEn: A price change moves you along the curve; income, tastes or substitute prices shift the whole curve.

points.v: 只有自身价格变化才导致需求量变化，其余因素不变。
points.vEn: Only the good's own price changes quantity demanded, holding everything else constant.

points.v: 收入上升、偏好转向、替代品涨价或买家人数增加都会推高需求。
points.vEn: Higher income, shifting tastes, pricier substitutes or more buyers all raise demand.

points.v: 互补品涨价、预期未来降价、替代品降价都会压低需求。
points.vEn: Pricier complements, expectations of future discounts or cheaper substitutes reduce demand.

points.v: 中文常混用，但前者指整条曲线，后者指某一价格下的具体数量。
points.vEn: Demand is the whole curve; quantity demanded is the amount at a given price.

watch: 把「价格上涨导致需求减少」和「需求减少导致价格下跌」混为一谈，是最常见的因果倒置。
观察到价格与数量同时上升，通常意味着供给或需求曲线发生了移动，而不是需求定律失效。
watchEn: Confusing 'higher price reduces demand' with 'lower demand reduces price' is a common reversal of causation.
Price and quantity rising together usually means a curve shifted, not that the law of demand failed.

title: 弹性与定价
lead: 涨价能否增加收入，取决于需求弹性；弹性小于 1 时涨价增收，大于 1 时涨价反而减收。
leadEn: Whether a price rise raises revenue depends on elasticity: below 1 it helps, above 1 it hurts.

points.v: 必需品、替代品少、占支出比例小 → 涨价后销量跌得少，收入增加。
points.vEn: Necessities with few substitutes and a small budget share lose few sales, so revenue rises.

points.v: 非必需、替代品多、比价方便 → 涨价后销量大跌，收入可能下降。
points.vEn: Discretionary goods with many substitutes lose sales sharply, so revenue can fall.

points.v: 短期难以改变习惯，长期可以换车、搬家、改配方，弹性上升。
points.vEn: Habits adjust slowly: over time people can switch cars or suppliers, raising elasticity.

points.v: 把不同弹性的人群分开（学生票、早鸟价），是提高总收入的标准做法。
points.vEn: Separating groups by elasticity — student fares, early-bird rates — is the standard way to raise revenue.

watch: 「涨价一定赚钱」只在缺乏弹性时成立，很多企业败在这里。
弹性是估算值而非精确常数，同一商品在不同时期、不同地区差异很大。
watchEn: 'Raising price always raises revenue' holds only when demand is inelastic; many firms get this wrong.
Elasticity is an estimate, not a constant: it varies by period and market.

title: 成本结构
lead: 固定成本、可变成本与边际成本决定企业的盈亏平衡点与最优产量。
leadEn: Fixed, variable and marginal costs determine a firm's break-even point and optimal output.

points.v: 与产量无关（厂房、软件研发、牌照），产量越大单件摊得越薄。
points.vEn: Independent of output (plants, software development, licences) and spread thinner as volume grows.

points.v: 随产量变化（原料、计件工资、运费）。
points.vEn: Scales with output: materials, piece-rate wages, freight.

points.v: 多做一件的增量成本；只要价格高于它，短期内继续生产就是合理的。
points.vEn: The extra cost of one more unit: while price exceeds it, producing on is rational in the short run.

points.v: 总贡献（价格 − 可变成本）覆盖固定成本时的产量即为平衡点。
points.vEn: The output at which total contribution (price minus variable cost) covers fixed cost.

watch: 固定成本高、边际成本低的行业（软件、内容、航空）天然趋向规模集中与价格战。
把已投入的固定成本当成「必须继续」的理由，就是沉没成本谬误。
watchEn: Industries with high fixed and low marginal costs (software, content, airlines) naturally concentrate and cut prices.
Treating spent fixed cost as a reason to continue is the sunk-cost fallacy.

sources.label: 平狄克、鲁宾费尔德《微观经济学》

title: 四种市场形态
lead: 从完全竞争到垄断，卖家数量与产品差异决定定价权，也决定对消费者与效率的影响。
leadEn: From perfect competition to monopoly, seller count and differentiation determine pricing power and welfare.

points.v: 众多小卖家、同质产品、自由进出，长期利润趋近于零。
points.vEn: Many small sellers of identical goods with free entry: long-run profit tends to zero.

points.v: 产品有差异（餐馆、服装），短期有定价权，长期因进入而摊薄。
points.vEn: Differentiated products (restaurants, apparel) give short-run pricing power that erodes with entry.

points.v: 少数几家彼此牵制，策略互动明显，可能默契维持高价。
points.vEn: A few interdependent players: strategic interaction can sustain high prices tacitly.

points.v: 单一卖家可定价，但受需求约束；若靠壁垒维持，需监管介入。
points.vEn: A single seller can set price, limited by demand; if sustained by barriers, regulation follows.

watch: 「集中度下降就一定有竞争」未必成立：地域、渠道或数据壁垒可能仍阻止有效竞争。
垄断并不总是坏事：自然垄断行业（电网、自来水管网）由一家提供反而成本最低。
watchEn: Falling concentration does not guarantee competition: geographic, channel or data barriers may persist.
Monopoly is not always harmful: in natural monopolies (grids, water networks) one provider is cheapest.

sources.label: 泰勒尔《产业组织理论》
sources.labelEn: Tirole, The Theory of Industrial Organization

title: 外部性的治理工具
lead: 庇古税、排污权交易、科斯式产权界定与直接管制各有适用条件与代价。
leadEn: Pigouvian taxes, permit trading, Coasean property rights and direct regulation each fit different conditions.

points.v: 按边际外部成本征税，把社会成本内化到价格中，简单但税率难定。
points.vEn: Taxing the marginal external cost internalises it, yet the right rate is hard to know.

points.v: 先定总量再让市场分配配额，减排成本低者多减、成本高者购买。
points.vEn: Cap the total and let the market allocate permits: cheap abaters cut more, costly ones buy.

points.v: 若交易成本低、产权清晰，双方可自行协商达成有效结果（科斯定理）。
points.vEn: With clear rights and low transaction costs, parties can bargain to an efficient outcome (Coase).

points.v: 标准、禁令、技术强制，执行确定但往往缺乏灵活性、成本更高。
points.vEn: Standards, bans and technology mandates are certain to enforce but inflexible and often costlier.

watch: 科斯定理的前提（产权清晰、交易成本低）在现实中常常不成立，因此不能一律「交给市场」。
总量控制的关键是配额初始分配方式，它决定了谁是赢家、谁是输家。
watchEn: Coase's premises — clear rights and low transaction costs — often fail, so 'leave it to the market' is not universal.
Under a cap, how permits are initially allocated decides who wins and who loses.

sources.label: 科斯《社会成本问题》
sources.labelEn: Coase, The Problem of Social Cost

title: 信息不对称
lead: 一方知道得更多，市场可能萎缩甚至消失，因为好商品被坏商品挤出。
leadEn: When one side knows more, markets can shrink or vanish as good products are driven out.

points.v: 交易前信息劣势方无法分辨质量，只愿出平均价，优质卖家退出。
points.vEn: Before contracting, the less informed side pays an average price, so high-quality sellers exit.

points.v: 交易后因有人兜底而改变行为，如参保后更不注意健康。
points.vEn: After contracting, protection changes behaviour, such as taking fewer health precautions once insured.

points.v: 有成本且难以伪造的信号（学历、认证、保修）能重建信任。
points.vEn: Costly, hard-to-fake signals (degrees, certification, warranties) rebuild trust.

points.v: 信息劣势方设计机制让不同类型自我暴露，如免赔额与自付比例。
points.vEn: The less informed side designs menus that make types reveal themselves, such as deductibles.

watch: 二手车、保险、信贷、招聘、医疗是信息不对称最典型的五个场景。
平台评级与第三方认证是数字时代的信号机制，但刷单会侵蚀其可信度。
watchEn: Used cars, insurance, credit, hiring and healthcare are the five classic arenas.
Platform ratings and third-party certification are modern signals, but fake reviews erode them.
